Current completeness requires report bone keys, and finite check requires finite components; neither check itself requires distinct hip/foot positions or nondegenerate axes.

If at least two wraps occur in captured phase, the first post-calibration interval is absent from those three measurements. This contradicts the adjacent peak-loop comment that every complete post-warmup cycle is independently gated. The old P17 source has the same nested warmup calls for terrain-classified data.

thirteen_lens_perspectives.bounded_assessment: P17 peak helper makes insufficient samples or missing neighborhoods unavailable and admits prominence as SignedLength; 95e returns scalar count/boolean and folds empty neighborhood to infinity. P17 pose uses checked result admission for each geometric observation and identifies degenerate axis; current opposite-leg min can mask undefined hemisphere under the stated condition.

A valid collection of independently finite transforms does not establish nondegenerate limb geometry or that every applicable axis contributed to the extremum; a gate must combine valid observation coverage with its numeric threshold. Phase peak count and window membership must cover required complete cycles.

P17 exact peak and pose objects are distinct from current peak body and inline pose metrics; absence of pose.rs path is proved, not interpreted as missing feature. Snapshot comparison does not establish chronological regression or runtime outcome.
Explicit checked geometric conversions, observation reasons, and local metric aggregation encode contract; there is no evidence that replacing these with generated derives would preserve semantics.

P17 distinguishes measured, unavailable and not-applicable while 95e retained metrics use primitive scalars. Preserve intentional nonprocedural no-IK exceptions separately from required geometry failure.

P17 HeightSample carries CyclePhase and SignedLength, pose uses BoneRole, AngularMagnitudeDegrees and NonnegativeLength. Native vector math may remain at geometric boundaries while existing owners govern unit/availability.

P17 validates signed prominence and rejects unavailable leg axes; 95e maps a failed normalization to infinity, which f32::min can discard in favor of another observation. A conditionally masked axis does not prove all report gates pass.

The 3mm prominence, 0.125-cycle neighbor search, 0.10 phase windows, 0.8 complete-cycle criterion and knee thresholds are report policies; their calibration and intended coverage remain owner questions, not defects merely because they are constants.

Assigned metric kernels use typed anatomical roles and no raw business string classification. Scenario label native output and scenario-producer admission belong to separate already recorded q1230; no new string finding.

Capture planned scenarios and metadata flow through scenario_metrics warmup, phase metrics/pose frames, then acceptance. Related prior P17-HEIGHT-DOUBLE-WARMUP retains original /root/rig_identity attribution, with double filtering conditional on wraps.

Peak count and passing-window flags derive from same samples while expected count is independent oracle; fixed report thresholds are not competing live state. Canonical calibration boundary should be explicit without erasing legitimate terrain treatment.

A nonapplicable scenario, undefined geometry, missing neighborhood and measured value represent distinct evidence conditions; angle, signed body position and nonnegative lengths also have different units and frames.

Native rig/animation owns produced transforms and limb axes; report metric owns measured availability and report validation owns applicability and acceptance. Central retains ledger alias decisions and downstream product-policy resolution.
